current_example.problem: Find a fraction that is equivalent to $\dfrac {\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{8}}$ that does not contain a radical in the denominator.
current_example.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{8}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{8}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{8}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{8}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{8}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{8}}{(\sqrt{8})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{8}}{8} & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we notice that $8$ has a perfect square factor $(4).$ Therefore, we can rewrite $\sqrt{8}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{8} & = \\ \sqrt{4\cdot 2} & = \\ \sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{2} & = \\ 2\sqrt{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify our original fraction as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{8}}{8} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot 2\sqrt{2}}{8} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot \sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{8} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{4} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5\cdot 2}}{4} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
